name: The Court House and City Hall (J. M. Van Osdel 1853; wings 1870), Court House square

grade.why: Pictured: a picture on the Images tab shows it.

documented_range.note: The wings and the added storey were completed during 1870 (Andreas vol. 2, p. 66; the day is not given, so the phase opens at the year's end), and the building burned on the morning of 9 October 1871 (vol. 2, pp. 368, 719).

change_note: Built T-3688 (2026-11-19): the Court House stands in the 1871 scene on the landmark_1871 archetype, from Lovejoy & Foster's 1871 stereograph and Andreas's engraving.

placement.position_note: The footprint's south-west corner (local E 475.74, N -348.83): the building is centred in the square as both pictures show it, the square being the block the 1871 plan's LaSalle, Clark, Randolph and Washington Streets enclose (lot lines E 474.4-566.0, N -384.3 to -273.0), squared to Washington Street (89.53 degrees). Good to the plan's tracing of Mitchell's map, a few metres. IT LAPS THE 1835 PLAT'S CLARK STREET BY ABOUT 3.3 m, AND THAT IS REFUSED IN WRITING, NOT REPAIRED (T-3688; tools/corridor_intrusion_baseline.json `refused`). The corridor is derived from the 1835 street control; the square is the 1871 plan's, traced from Mitchell's 1870 map, which is what the 1871 scene draws. The two tracings disagree by about 4 m here, and moving the building 3.3 m west to clear the older one would take it off the centre of the square both pictures show it on.
placement.symbolic_location: The middle of the Court House square, bounded by Clark, Randolph, LaSalle and Washington Streets.

footprint.note: The building's outline, 89.24 by 39.62 m overall: the 1853 house's 100-foot main part with its north and south porticoes 60 feet wide (130 feet north to south, Andreas vol. 1, p. 181), and the two 1870 wings against its east and west sides, each 80 feet east to west and 130 north to south, the planned wing's size in the Chicago Evening Post of 2 October 1868, with a pavilion breaking 5 m forward from the middle of each wing's street front, as the stereograph shows the Clark Street one (its width and projection read through the fitted camera; the LaSalle Street one is taken as its twin, reconstructed). The wings take in the 1853 house's east and west projections (32 by 60 feet), which the fit leaves no room for beside them (T-3688).

fire.note: The cupola caught about midnight; the watchmen left the tower about 1:30 and the great bell fell through the building at 2:05 a.m. on 9 October 1871; the walls of the wings stood as a shell (Andreas vol. 2, pp. 368, 719).

towers.name: the cupola
towers.note: The great cupola on the middle of the 1853 house, its round drum of tall arched openings under the fire watch's balustraded gallery, then the clock stage and the ribbed dome with its lantern and staff, as the stereograph shows it through its fitted camera; the gallery stands 36 m up, the 'observatory balcony ... one hundred and twenty feet from the ground' (Chicago Illustrated, 1866, quoted by Chicagology).

value.note: Each part is read off the Lovejoy & Foster stereograph and Andreas's plate, scaled on the 1853 house's 100-foot front (Andreas vol. 1, p. 181); where a part has its own grade its note says what else it rests on.

composition.note: THE 1853 HOUSE (Andreas vol. 1, p. 181: Lockport gray marble, the main part 100 feet square, porticoes north and south with stone steps): a rusticated basement and three storeys after the storey added in 1870 (vol. 2, p. 66), round-headed windows below and square above, the porticoes carrying low pediments, a low roof; on it THE CUPOLA, a square base, then a round drum of tall arched openings with a balustraded gallery (the fire watch's), a second drum with the clock and a ribbed dome with a lantern and staff, as the stereograph shows it; and the smaller octagonal belfry with a bell-shaped cap and the small domed cupola beside it (vol. 1: 'two domes and a cupola'). THE WINGS of 1870 (Lemont stone, vol. 2, p. 66): a rusticated basement and three storeys of round-arched windows with moulded heads, a bracketed cornice and balustraded parapet, a projecting centre pavilion on the north and south fronts crowned by a scrolled crest, and low domes on the corners. Storey heights and the wings' bays are read off the stereograph against the 1853 house's 100-foot front (reconstructed where the pictures cannot say).

wall_material.note: The original building of marble from the Lockport quarries of New York; the additions of stone from the Lemont quarries of Cook County (Andreas vol. 2, p. 66). Both built in the K02 library's limestones: the 1853 house darkened by smoke and the 1870 wings still pale, as the stereograph of 1871 shows them.

function.note: The joint building of the city and the county since 1853: the county's courts and offices in the east half, the city's in the west half, bought by the city in the enlargement of 1869-1870 (Andreas vol. 2, p. 66).

built.note: Completed 1853 by the city and county (Andreas vol. 1, p. 181; vol. 2, p. 66); its two wings and an additional storey were added in 1869-1870 and completed during 1870 (vol. 2, p. 66).

research_note: THE COURT HOUSE, built by T-3688 for the 1871 scene. From Lovejoy & Foster's stereograph of 1871 from Clark and Randolph Streets and Andreas's engraving 'The Court-House before the fire' (vol. 2, p. 65) from Clark and Washington: the 1853 house of Lockport marble in the middle under its domed cupola with the fire watch's balcony and the clock, a smaller octagonal belfry and domed cupola on its roof, and the two Lemont-stone wings of 1870 east and west, each with a scrolled crest over its centre pavilion and low domes on its corners. The plan sizes are the 1853 house's (Andreas vol. 1, p. 181) and the planned wing's in the Chicago Evening Post of 2 October 1868 (80 by 130 feet); the wings' fronts, height and street pavilions are read off the stereograph through its fitted camera (docs/LIBERTIES.md, T-3688).
